title: 「Not until ... did ...」倒裝句

omissions: Every numbered Important Rule and Benefit is retained as a separate Chinese-primary card. Where the PDF has no complete English counterpart, the English explanation is a faithful editorial translation.
The source filename is numbered 218; it is assigned system ID ss219 because the source set contains two distinct PDFs labelled 201.

formula: Not until + past time / past event + did + subject + base verb + other information

formulas.formula: Not until + past time / past event + did + subject + base verb + other information

example: Not until the final meeting did the team realise how serious the issue was.
exampleZh: 直到最後一次會議，團隊才意識到問題有多嚴重。

examples.en: Not until the final meeting did the team realise how serious the issue was.
examples.zh: 直到最後一次會議，團隊才意識到問題有多嚴重。
examples.highlight: Not until the final meeting did the team realise how serious the issue was.

meaning.zh: 這個句型表示某件事情在某個時間或事件發生之前一直沒有發生，直到那一刻才發生。

rules.zh: 必須放在句首 一般句： The team did not realise how serious the issue was until the final meeting. 倒裝句： Not until the final meeting did the team realise how serious the issue was.
rules.en: Place Not until at the beginning. Compare the ordinary sentence “The team did not realise how serious the issue was until the final meeting” with the inverted form “Not until the final meeting did the team realise how serious the issue was.”

rules.zh: 主句必須使用倒裝語序 一般語序： the team realised 倒裝語序： did the team realise 正確： Not until Friday did Daniel finish the report. 錯誤： Not until Friday Daniel finished the report.
rules.en: Use inversion in the main clause: did + subject + base verb. Write “Not until Friday did Daniel finish the report”, not “Not until Friday Daniel finished the report.”

rules.zh: 後面必須使用動詞原形 正確： did the team realise did Sarah understand did the bus arrive 錯誤： did the team realised did Sarah understood did the bus arrived
rules.en: Use the base form after did: did the team realise, did Sarah understand and did the bus arrive, not realised, understood or arrived.

rules.zh: 後面的部分不使用倒裝 正確： Not until the rain stopped did the children go outside. 錯誤： Not until did the rain stop the children go outside. 只有主句需要倒裝；until 後面的時間從句保持正常語序。
rules.en: Do not invert the clause after until. Only the main clause is inverted: “Not until the rain stopped did the children go outside.”

rules.zh: 主句不需要再加入 not Not until 本身已經帶有否定意思。 正確： Not until midnight did the bus arrive. 錯誤： Not until midnight did the bus not arrive.
rules.en: Do not add not to the inverted main clause because Not until already carries the negative meaning. Write “Not until midnight did the bus arrive.”

rules.zh: 這個句型表示「直到……才……」 Not until the teacher explained it again did I understand. 這句不是表示「我一直理解」，而是表示老師再次解釋之前，我一直不明白。
rules.en: The structure means “only when that time or event was reached”. It shows that the action had not happened before that point.

rules.zh: 本課只練習過去式 did 倒裝 本課接受： Not until + past time or event + did + subject + base verb 本課不包括： Not until tomorrow will we know the result. Not until recently has the problem become clear. Not until then was he ready. 以上句子可以正確，但使用了其他時態或助動詞，不屬於本課的目標句型。
rules.en: This lesson practises past-time inversion with did only. Forms with will, has or was may be grammatical, but they are outside this lesson’s target.

rules.zh: 本練習不接受以下非倒裝答案 It was not until Friday that Daniel finished the report. Daniel did not finish the report until Friday. 以上句子意思相近，但沒有使用本課要求的 Not until ... did ... 倒裝結構。
rules.en: Use the required inverted form. Similar non-inverted alternatives such as “It was not until ... that ...” or an ordinary “did not ... until ...” sentence are not accepted in this exercise.

benefits.zh: 這個句型能清楚指出，事情究竟到了哪個時間或發生哪件事之後才出現變化。
benefits.en: It makes the timing very clear. This structure clearly identifies the exact time or event that finally caused a change.

benefits.zh: 把 Not until 放在句首，可以突出事情比預期更遲發生，或經過一段時間後才發生。 比較： The team did not understand the problem until the final meeting. Not until the final meeting did the team understand the problem. 第二句更強調「直到最後一次會議才明白」。
benefits.en: It emphasises a delay. Putting Not until at the beginning draws attention to how late something happened.

benefits.zh: 讀者會先看到事情一直沒有發生，然後才知道最後出現甚麼結果，因此能增加故事的懸念。
benefits.en: It can create suspense in a story. The reader first learns about the delay and then discovers what finally happened.

benefits.zh: 這個句型能清楚連接兩件事情，表示第一件事發生後，第二件事才出現。
benefits.en: It connects two events clearly. The structure shows that the first event had to happen before the second event could take place.

benefits.zh: 你不需要每次都以人物或事物開始句子，也可以先提出最重要的時間或事件，增加句式變化。
benefits.en: It gives you another way to organise a sentence. You can begin with the important time or event instead of always beginning with the person or thing performing the action.

benefits.zh: 這個句型適合用於故事、報告和較正式的寫作，尤其適合描述發現、延遲的決定、轉捩點和重要 領悟。
benefits.en: It is useful in stories, reports and formal writing, especially for discoveries, delayed decisions, turning points and important realisations.
